subject: Post-call: Finsight data handling / subprocessors clarifications
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Elena Novak <elena.novak@finsight.ai>, Samir Rao <samir@finsight.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call: Finsight data handling / subprocessors clarifications

Hi Elena / Samir — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side and a few follow-ups so we can scope the pilot and the security review: 

Recap (from our 45m discovery):
- Primary use: text extraction and embeddings for search + user-facing summarization.
- Data types discussed: user-generated content (documents, messages) + user IDs and account metadata.
- Compliance ask: audit log retention, ability to restrict third-party telemetry, and data residency in the US.

Open items / asks (can you confirm these?):
1) PII definition: do you consider hashed user IDs (deterministic) to be PII for this project?
2) Retention target: you mentioned audit retention ~12 months — please confirm whether logs or full payloads need to be kept for 12 months.
3) Subprocessors: we discussed telemetry vendors and cloud provider monitoring. Please list any vendors that cannot receive even pseudonymized telemetry (for contract gating).
4) Logging controls: do you require application payloads to be redacted before retention, or is access-control + audit sufficient?

What we'll provide by EOD Monday:
- brief subprocessor inventory with data scopes (redwood-subprocessors-2028-03.csv)
- a one-page dataflow diagram showing which telemetry events are sent to third parties
- SOC2 report and retention defaults doc

Attachments: call recording + draft mutual action plan (MAP) for pilot (see attached).

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm Q1–Q3 above by Mon 3/13 so we can finalize the pilot SOW and get legal looped in.
- Schedule a 30m technical follow-up (SRE + security) w/ Marissa and Karthik — suggested times Tue/Wed next week.

Thanks,
Ava Chen

ava.chen@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Mar 2028 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Finsight data handling / subprocessors clarifications

Thanks for the recap — a couple quick technical clarifications we should surface to Elena: 

- Redwood default telemetry/operational logs retention is 30 days; for Dedicated/Enterprise we can extend to 90/365 days depending on the contract (config + storage delta). Need finance to confirm exact pricing for 12 months.
- We do not log full request payloads by default to external telemetry vendors; request-level traces are sampled and sensitive fields (by default keys named password/ssn/email) are redacted before uplink. However, customers can opt-in to richer telemetry for debugging — worth confirming they do NOT want that.
- For embeddings and KV cache: KV cache entries are kept in ephemeral GPU memory and are not persisted to third-party telemetry.

I'll draft a short note on the retention tiers and attach to the subprocessor inventory. Marissa — can you handle legal gating on any vendor that Finsight marks as disallowed?

-Karthik
Principal Engineer, Product Reliability | Redwood Inference

From: Elena Novak <elena.novak@finsight.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Samir Rao <samir@finsight.ai>
Cc: security@finsight.ai
Date: Mon, 13 Mar 2028 08:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Finsight data handling / subprocessors clarifications

Hi Ava / team — thanks for the notes. A few clarifications from security so we can decide whether to move forward with the pilot: 

1) PII: We treat any identifier that can be linked back to a natural person as PII, including deterministic hashed IDs if they can be re-identified (so hashed IDs are in scope).
2) Retention: For audit reasons we require event-level logs that show access and major state changes to be retained 12 months. We do NOT require full application payloads to be retained for 12 months — those should be purged after 30 days unless redaction is applied.
3) Subprocessors: We cannot permit raw user payloads to be forwarded to any third party. Pseudonymized telemetry (metrics, counters, anonymized latency pings) is acceptable if contractually bound and if no user-level identifiers are included. Please provide a list of subprocessors and the data class each receives.
4) Data residency: US-only for this pilot. Any backup or analytics export must remain on US-hosted infrastructure.

We'd like the redwood subprocessor inventory and a short dataflow diagram by EOD Wed 3/15. Also please include whether you use any managed telemetry agents that send telemetry outside of Redwood infra (e.g., marketplace integrations).

If you can send the doc I can route to procurement/legal for contract gating. Also proposing a 30m follow-up Wed 3/15 10:00am PT.

Thanks,
Elena Novak
Head of Security | FinSight Analytics
elena.novak@finsight.ai
